reason: I'll start with the after-meal condition to see how pancreatic cells respond to abundant glucose.
expectation: I expect the beta cells to release insulin into the blood, initiating glucose storage or uptake.

alternatives.reason: The between-meals response is also relevant, but I prefer to follow the meal first.

effect: The beta cells released insulin, which reaches both muscle and liver; I can follow either target.
reaction: The separate branches make the next choices clear.
reason: I'll follow insulin to skeletal muscle to see how it handles glucose after a meal.
expectation: I expect insulin to increase glucose uptake by muscle, possibly with some glucose stored as glycogen.

alternatives.reason: The liver is another insulin target, but I'll follow muscle first.

effect: Insulin increases muscle glucose transport, and its release weakens as blood glucose falls; I will follow its liver branch next.
reaction: The transporter and feedback details make the response clearer.
reason: The liver is the other target of the after-meal insulin signal.
expectation: I expect insulin to promote glucose storage as glycogen in the liver.

alternatives.reason: The between-meals response also matters, but I want to finish the after-meal branch first.

effect: Insulin favours liver glycogen storage and reduces glucose output, completing the after-meal goal; the between-meals response remains.
reaction: The distinction from muscle transporter insertion is useful.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it starts the between-meals branch.
expectation: I expect pancreatic alpha cells to release glucagon into the blood, signalling the liver to release glucose.

effect: The between-meal condition increases glucagon release and decreases insulin; the remaining action follows glucagon to the liver.
reaction: The contrasting alpha- and beta-cell responses make the comparison clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination and follows the glucagon signal to its liver target.
expectation: I expect glucagon to promote glycogen breakdown and glucose release into the blood.

effect: Glucagon promotes liver glycogen breakdown and glucose release, with stimulation diminishing as glucose rises; both goals are complete.
reaction: The feedback completes the comparison clearly, though the result was expected.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following insulin to muscle was worthwhile: the transporter change connects a bloodborne signal to glucose uptake and feedback.

leastWorthwhile.text: The pancreatic sensing steps were predictable from the two conditions, although they established the comparison.

surprise.text: The liver panel explicitly distinguished its glucose entry from muscle's transporter insertion, sharpening the comparison between insulin targets.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, but the final two were the only offered combinations, so they involved little choice.

continue.text: I would continue for another chapter if it offered a similarly clear comparison, though the predictable, mostly guided combinations limit the gameplay interest.
